acceptance_rule: Correctness, originality, and value must all pass.

correctness.rationale: The infinite proof was reconstructed from the package rather than inferred from its prior verdict. Menon–Singh path concatenation reduces every tree coefficientwise to a three-arm spider. For a spider \(S(a,b,c)\), the stated formulas \(z(2)=9-2t\) and \(z(3)=13n-66+2r\) give the first two case separations, while the fort argument separates \(A_n\) from \(B_n\) at size \(n-4\). An independent zero-forcing enumerator for \(n=11,12\) reproduced the critical counts, including \(z(A_{11};7)=329<330=z(B_{11};7)\) and \(z(A_{12};8)=494<495=z(B_{12};8)\). The finite check is corroboration; the case split and fort arguments establish all \(n\ge11\).
correctness.risks: The proof is for the tree subposet and does not identify all coatoms or claim a universal runner-up outside trees.

broader_coverage.evidence: Path-extremal theorems only give the top element; Li–Cao–Ji (2025) studies forcing-number differences and does not determine polynomial coefficient counts.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Knowing the unique top class does not determine the coatoms or exclude a universal second-best nonpath tree.
broader_coverage.search: tree path-extremal theorems; outerplanar path domination; extremal forcing problems of trees

checked_sources: semantic search of the public findings corpus

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: Those results provide the monotone path-concatenation operation and top-class extremality but not the package's three-case obstruction among nonpaths.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: An additional analysis of three-arm spiders and small forts is required to derive the final claim.
claim_vs_prior_implication.search: Menon–Singh Proposition 3.13/Corollary 3.14 and Boyer et al. polynomial results

equivalent_formulations.evidence: Menon–Singh formulate the coefficientwise poset and explicitly ask about coatoms below the path.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A greatest nonpath polynomial class is exactly a universal runner-up beneath the path in the tree subposet, so this search targets the same statement rather than a title match.
equivalent_formulations.search: zero-forcing polynomial coefficientwise tree poset; coatoms; universal second-best tree; spider extremizers

exact_database_or_table.evidence: No published table was found that states the all-order \(n\ge11\) obstruction. Small-order enumeration only corroborates initial cases.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The claim is an infinite structural theorem, not a finite-table consequence.
exact_database_or_table.search: small-tree zero-forcing polynomial tables and fort catalogues

originality.rationale: The closest primary source proves path domination for trees and then explicitly asks what the coatoms below the path are; it does not answer the runner-up question. Boyer et al. introduce the polynomial but do not contain this second-level extremal theorem. A directly relevant 2025 paper on extremal forcing problems of trees was inspected in full and concerns zero, total, and connected forcing numbers rather than coefficient counts. Searches of the public findings corpus found the audited theorem itself and later, different zero-forcing extremal results, but no earlier theorem implying this pair-of-spiders obstruction.
originality.residual_risks: A non-indexed specialist note could contain an equivalent coatom analysis, but the principal paper that introduced the current tree extremal question explicitly leaves it open.

source_inspections.assessment: Supplies the reduction and explicitly leaves the audited second-level extremal question open.
source_inspections.material_read: full open article, including Proposition 3.13, Corollary 3.14, and the concluding poset/coatom question

source_inspections.assessment: Concerns zero/total/connected forcing numbers, not zero-forcing polynomial coefficients or coatoms.
Introduces and studies the zero-forcing polynomial; no coverage of the audited tree coatom theorem found.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a natural next extremal question explicitly posed after path domination, and does so uniformly for every \(n\ge11\) with a concrete two-witness obstruction. Determining the second layer of a natural coefficientwise poset is a motivated structural result rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
value.risks: It proves nonexistence of a universal second-best tree rather than a complete classification of all coatoms.

final_claim: For every integer \(n\ge 11\), the coefficientwise poset of zero-forcing polynomials of nonpath \(n\)-vertex trees has no greatest element; explicitly the spiders \(A_n=S(2,2,n-5)\) and \(B_n=S(2,4,n-7)\) witness a strict loss for every nonpath tree in one of the coefficients \(2\), \(3\), or \(n-4\), so at least two coatoms lie below the path class.
